beatOutlines.textOutline: Monday morning, Raju connected two low points on Kesar Paints and drew a line.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji looked at the screen and asked: did price respect it a third time?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju said: why wait for a third time? From the ₹148 peak it came right to ₹140!
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Look at the chart. The share climbed from ₹98 to a high of ₹148 on candle 16.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju bought at ₹140 support, but there was no bounce and the line broke.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Price broke ₹140 and fell to ₹134, because that line was not valid yet.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Today we learn the difference between tentative and valid lines, and the rule of three.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Next we explore the 45-degree slope, plus 3% price and 2-day time filters.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Then we see how broken trendlines reverse roles and how the fan principle works.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Finally, we learn to use channel lines to spot profit targets and trend strength.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Connecting any two lows draws a line, but Murphy calls this only a tentative line.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Only when price touches and bounces off the line a third time does it become valid.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The number three is vital in technical analysis: three touches, three fan lines, three peaks.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Not all slopes are equal. If a line is too steep, over 60 degrees, it cannot last.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Conversely, if the line is too flat, buyers lack conviction and the trend is weak.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The most sustainable uptrend runs at 45 degrees, where price and time advance in balance.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sometimes intraday price dips below a line but closes above it. That is a false break.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The first defense is the 3% price filter: closing price must penetrate the line by 3%.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second defense is the 2-day time filter: price must close beyond the line for two days.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When a valid ₹140 support line finally breaks, the buyer-seller balance flips completely.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When price drops to ₹134 and rallies back to ₹140 from below, trapped buyers rush to exit.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Because of this psychology, a decisively broken support line becomes new resistance.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now see the Fan Principle. After ₹158 and the ₹175 peak, the first steep trendline breaks.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: We draw a flatter second line. After the ₹156 bounce at candle 20, it breaks too.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When the third fan line breaks at ₹142, price drops to ₹134 confirming a full trend reversal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Often price trends between two parallel lines: the basic trendline and a channel line.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Traders buy the lower line and take profits when price hits the ₹158 channel roof.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Stalling at ₹158 signals weakness, sending price down to the lower line at ₹141.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now your turn. Read this scenario carefully and apply Murphy's trendline rules.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think: three fan lines, the 3% filter, and the 2-day rule—what do they say?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Correct! Breaking the third fan line past both filters confirms a valid trend reversal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The next day, Raju understood his mistake and showed Sharma ji his updated chart.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji smiled and asked: now that it dropped to ₹134, what happens at ₹140 on a bounce?
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju replied: Role reversal! Old support turns into resistance, and I will watch the third fan line.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Let us tie together all seven core principles from today's chapter.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Two points draw a tentative line; only a third successful bounce makes it valid.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: A 45-degree slope is most sustainable, while 3% and 2-day filters stop whipsaws.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Broken support becomes resistance, and breaking the third fan line confirms reversal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Channel lines mark targets. Draw with two, confirm with three, and filter every break.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Two touches draw a tentative trendline
A third touch and bounce validates the trendline
3% price and 2-day time filters prevent false breaks
Role reversal turns broken support into resistance
Breaking the 3rd fan line confirms trend reversal
Parallel channel lines mark targets and momentum shifts
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
